name: autocad_adjudicate

verdicts.point: Scale calibration (mm-per-px) used for all measurements
verdicts.verdict: 1 original px = 0.7812 mm (1.2802 px/mm). Working at 6x LANCZOS upsample: 7.681 px6/mm. Established independently from four labeled circles and mutually consistent to sigma = 0.08%, so it is not a free parameter that could be tuned to favor either reading.
verdicts.evidence: Least-squares (Kasa) circle fits on the 6x ink mask, all with 360/360 angular bin coverage: O40 hub outer r=153.62 px6 -> 7.681 px6/mm; O20 hub bore r=76.87 -> 7.687; O50 boss outer r=192.10 -> 7.684; O16 boss bore r=61.37 -> 7.671. Mean 7.681, std 0.006 (0.08%). Ratio check: 153.62/76.87 = 1.999 == 40/20, and 192.10/61.37 = 3.130 == 50/16 (3.125). Fitted centers: C1 = (2069.59, 762.85) px6 = (344.93, 127.14) orig px; C2 = (1992.57, 1250.91) px6 = (332.10, 208.49) orig px. Image is 474x266 px; the dimensioned reference sketch occupies the right (Paint 3D) panel, approx x[235,437] y[48,241].

verdicts.point: 1. C2 (O50/O16 boss) Y position below C1: ~48.3 mm (Reading A) or ~62 mm (Reading B)?
verdicts.verdict: READING B WINS. Measured offset C2 - C1 = (dx = -10.03 mm, dy = -63.54 mm) in CAD coordinates (y up), i.e. C2 = (-10.03, -63.54). The vertical drop is ~63.5 mm, decisively NOT ~48.3 mm. Reading A is wrong by 15.2 mm. Both readings agree on dx = -10, which the drawing labels explicitly as '10' and which measures -10.03 mm (0.03 mm error) - this confirms the scale is right and isolates the disagreement to Y alone.
verdicts.evidence: Center-to-center vector from the two least-squares circle fits: C2 - C1 = (-77.02, +488.06) px6 = (-12.837, +81.343) orig px. Dividing by 7.681 px6/mm gives dx = -10.028 mm, dy = 63.543 mm downward. Error vs Reading A (48.3): 15.24 mm = 117.1 px6 = 19.5 ORIGINAL pixels. Error vs Reading B (62): 1.54 mm = 2.0 original pixels. A 19.5-original-pixel discrepancy on a 474x266 image is roughly 3x the stroke width of the outline and is far outside any plausible measurement noise; the 2.0 px residual for Reading B is within it. Hypothesis sweep of predicted dy in px6 vs the measured 488.1: dy=48.3 -> 371.0 (miss by 117); dy=60 -> 460.9; dy=62 -> 476.2 (miss by 12); dy=63.5 -> 487.7 (miss by 0.4). Visual overlay confirmation: a marker placed at C1 + (-10, -48.3) mm lands in blank white space clearly ABOVE the boss, inside no circle at all, while a marker at C1 + (-10, -63.54) mm lands exactly on the center of the O16 bore where the horizontal and vertical red centerlines of the boss intersect. The true value is nearer 63.5 than 62, so Reading B's R32-tangency derivation is directionally correct and ~1.5 mm low, but it is unambiguously the correct reading of the two.

verdicts.point: 2. Curved slot S1 angular span about C1: 138-180 deg (Reading B) or 117-159 deg (Reading A)?
verdicts.verdict: READING B WINS. The slot occupies 138 deg to ~181 deg measured CCW from the +X axis at C1, terminating exactly on the horizontal centerline at 180 deg. Reading A's 117-159 deg window is empty over its first ~20 deg (117-135 deg is bare white paper) and misses the entire 159-180 deg portion of the real slot. Both readings agree the included angle is ~42 deg, which the drawing labels '42 deg'; the dispute is purely the phase, and it is 138-180, not 117-159.
verdicts.evidence: Radius histogram of ink in the angular window 120-195 deg about C1 shows sharp isolated peaks at exactly the expected slot radii, validating the R70/R78/R62 interpretation: R62-63 mm bin = 3169 px, R77-78 mm bin = 3940 px, and the arm outer edge at R84-86 = 5461 px. Contiguous-run analysis of these arcs (0.5 deg bins, gap tolerance 2 deg) gives: slot OUTER wall R78 present 135.5 -> 184.0 deg; slot INNER wall R62 present 135.0 -> 182.5 deg; arm outer edge R85 present 133.5 -> 186.5 deg. (The 1-4 deg overshoot past 180 and undershoot before 138 is the R8 end-cap arcs bulging beyond the wall extent plus stroke width, exactly as expected for a slot whose walls run 138-180 with R8 caps.) Direct endpoint probing of the 5x5 px6 neighborhood on both walls is decisive - on the R62 inner wall: 117 deg -> min gray 255 (BLANK), 120 deg -> 255 (BLANK), 130 deg -> 250 (BLANK), 135 deg -> 170 (BLANK), 138 deg -> 0 (INK), 150 deg -> 56 (INK), 159 deg -> 56 (INK), 170 deg -> 78 (INK), 180 deg -> 74 (INK), 183 deg -> 198 (BLANK). Identical pattern on the R78 outer wall: blank at 117/120/130/135, solid ink at 138 through 180, blank again at 183. Visual overlay: an R70 centerline arc drawn over 117-159 deg exits the top of the slot and runs across empty paper outside the part, whereas the same arc drawn over 138-180 deg lies perfectly inside the slot channel for its whole length.

verdicts.point: 3. KEY QUESTION: is the lower-right obround (R8 caps, ~30 long, at 135 deg) an INTERNAL SLOT (cut-out hole) or the EXTERNAL boundary of the third lobe?
verdicts.verdict: READING B WINS DECISIVELY. The obround is the EXTERNAL BOUNDARY of the third lobe - a stadium-shaped ear that IS the part outline there. It is NOT an internal slot or hole. Proven topologically: the obround's flanks and caps belong to the SAME connected thick-ink stroke as the R85 arm outer edge and the O50 boss outer circle, i.e. it is literally part of the single continuous outer profile. By direct contrast, the S1 curved slot's R78/R62 walls form their OWN separate isolated closed loop - that is what a real internal slot looks like in this same drawing, and the obround does not look like it. Reading A's characterization of it as an 'S2 slot' is wrong, as is its placement.
verdicts.evidence:
PRIMARY PROOF - connected-component labeling of thick strokes only (ink < 150 gray, 5x5 neighborhood density >= 18, 8-connectivity) cleanly separates the drawing into distinct components, and membership is unambiguous (60/60 sample points per element): R85 arm outer arc 138-180 deg -> component 91; O50 boss outer ring -> component 91; OBROUND flanks + caps -> component 91 (88/100 sample points, remainder being the tangent merge zones); R78 slot outer wall -> component 99; R62 slot inner wall -> component 99; O40 hub ring -> component 125; O20 bore and O16 bore -> their own separate loops. Component 91 has bbox x[235,437] y[48,241] orig px - it spans the ENTIRE drawing, which is the signature of one continuous outer profile, and the obround is welded into it. If the obround were a hole it would be its own small closed loop like component 99 (bbox x[244,288] y[57,137]) or component 125 (bbox x[318,371] y[101,153]); it is not.

SECONDARY PROOF - the caps are not closed circles. Angular occupancy of each R8 cap arc: NEAR cap has ink over 15-255 deg (240 deg of arc) with a 256-359 deg gap; FAR cap has ink over 195-75 deg through zero (239 deg) with a 77-194 deg gap. Both caps expose ~240 deg of arc facing OUTWARD away from the part body, and each missing sector points precisely along the axis toward the other cap - exactly where the two straight flanks attach. An internal slot cap would be a fully closed 360 deg loop (like the O16 and O20 bores, which fit at cov = 1.00); these are open arcs terminating tangentially into flanks. 

TERTIARY PROOF - nothing encloses it. Probing the normals outward from the obround axis: both straight flanks are 25/25 fully inked at exactly +/-R8 from the axis, but stepping outward the ink collapses immediately - at R8+1.0 mm only 5/20 and 3/20 sample points hit ink, at R8+2.0 mm 3/20 and 5/20, at R8+3.3 mm 2/20 and 5/20, at R8+5.2 mm 2/20 and 4/20, at R8+7.8 mm 1/20 and 0/20. Those few residual hits are thin dimension/centerline crossings (the 30 and 135 deg witness lines), not a boundary. There is NO thick continuous outline running around the outside of the obround; the outermost thick ink in that whole region IS the obround's own cap. At 14x magnification the long straight '60' flank is seen running down from upper-left and MERGING TANGENTIALLY into the obround's far cap, and the R25 concave fillet arc is seen sweeping in from the lower-left and merging tangentially into the obround's near-side flank - the outline enters and leaves the obround rather than passing around it.

GEOMETRIC CONFIRMATION of Reading B's exact placement, all within noise: near cap center measured at (399.6, 181.7) orig px vs Reading B's predicted (399.2, 181.5) - error 0.4 px; far cap center measured (426.2, 208.1) vs predicted (426.4, 208.6) - error 0.5 px; cap radii fit 8.20 and 8.28 mm vs R8 labeled; cap-to-cap distance 225.1 px6 = 29.31 mm vs 30 labeled (0.7 mm); axis bearing -44.75 deg vs -45 deg; distance C1 -> near cap center 60.3 mm vs the labeled '60' (0.3 mm); bearing C1 -> near cap -44.94 deg vs -45 deg (0.06 deg). Every one of Reading B's obround predictions is confirmed.

verdicts.point: Corroborating check on Reading B's remaining outer-chain claims (not disputed, reported for completeness)
verdicts.verdict: SUPPORTED. The R30 crest arc concentric with C1 is confirmed, which in turn confirms Reading B's claim that the O40 hub is a FREE-STANDING RING that the outer boundary passes OVER rather than being tangent to.
verdicts.evidence: An arc of radius 30 mm about C1 sampled over 30-90 deg lies on the outer-profile component at 80/80 = 100% of sample points. Since the O40 hub ring has radius 20 mm about the same center C1, the boundary crest at R30 stands off 10 mm outside the hub ring, so the ring is enclosed by the profile rather than forming it - it is a separate closed loop (component 125), consistent with the labeling result. The R32 and R25 fillets were probed by tangency construction against the O50 boss (fillet center at 25+32 = 57 mm and 25+25 = 50 mm from C2 respectively) and returned best inner-side arc occupancies of 0.57 and 0.60 at plausible bearings - consistent with fillets being present at those radii but not a tight enough fit to pin the exact construction, so this sub-claim is reported as plausible-unconfirmed rather than proven. It does not bear on the three adjudicated questions.

notes: OVERALL: Reading B (this session) is correct on all three disputed points; Reading A (last session) is wrong on all three. Method: the source is a small 474x266 JPEG screenshot showing an AutoCAD window (left) beside the dimensioned reference sketch in Paint 3D (right); all measurements were taken on the right panel, which is the clean dimensioned drawing. The image was upsampled 6x with LANCZOS and analysed with least-squares circle fitting, radial/angular ink histograms, direct grayscale endpoint probing, and 8-connectivity component labeling of thick strokes. Scale was calibrated from four labeled circles (O40, O20, O50, O16) agreeing to 0.08%, giving 0.7812 mm per original pixel; because the '10' horizontal offset between C1 and C2 reproduces to 0.03 mm, the calibration is independently validated and the large Y disagreement cannot be a scale artifact. Red-centerline color detection was attempted first but abandoned: JPEG compression at this resolution leaves max redness (R - (G+B)/2) of only 21.5 with the 99.9th percentile at 10.8, so the centerlines are not reliably separable by hue; centers were instead recovered from the concentric circle fits themselves, which is more accurate anyway (both hub and boss fits achieved full 360-degree angular coverage). CAVEAT / CORRECTION TO READING B: the measured C2 vertical offset is 63.54 mm, not the 62 mm that Reading B derived from R32 tangency - Reading B is about 1.5 mm (2 original px) low. The drawing carries no explicit vertical dimension between C1 and C2 (only the horizontal '10'), so this distance is a derived/constrained value; a rebuild should treat ~63.5 mm as the measured target and revisit the R32 tangency chain, or better, solve C2 from the full tangency network rather than a single fillet. Similarly the obround cap-to-cap distance measures 29.31 mm against a labeled 30, and the S1 walls read 135.5-184 deg against a nominal 138-180 - both are stroke-width and end-cap bleed effects of roughly one original pixel and should be snapped to the labeled nominal values (30, and 138-180 with a 42 deg included angle) when reconstructing. Labeled dimensions transcribed from the drawing: R85, R70, 42 deg, R8, R15, R32, O40, O20, R30 (x2), 10, O16, O50, R25, R8, 60, 30, 135 deg. Note the drawing carries TWO R30 callouts and TWO R8 callouts - one R8 for the S1 curved-slot end caps and one R8 for the external obround ear caps - which is a plausible source of Reading A's confusion in treating the obround as a second internal slot.
